legend: A subarray of an array B%%ZSMJ0%% is a contiguous sequence of elements taken from B%%ZSMJ1%%. For example, if B=[3,1,4,1,5]%%ZSMJ2%%, then [3,1,4]%%ZSMJ3%%, [4,1]%%ZSMJ4%%, the empty array [ ]%%ZSMJ5%% and the whole array B%%ZSMJ6%% are subarrays of B%%ZSMJ7%% (among others), while [3,4,5]%%ZSMJ8%% and [1,3]%%ZSMJ9%% are not subarrays of B%%ZSMJ10%%.

We also define Cm%%ZSMJ11%% as the array obtained by the concatenation of m%%ZSMJ12%% copies of the array C%%ZSMJ13%%. For example, if C=[3,2]%%ZSMJ14%% then C1=[3,2]%%ZSMJ15%%, C2=[3,2,3,2]%%ZSMJ16%% and C∞=[…,3,2,3,2,3,2,…]%%ZSMJ17%%.
In this problem you are given an array P%%ZSMJ18%% containing no repeated numbers, and you have to process a sequence of events that occur in order. The events can be of three types:

Delete:  a number present in P%%ZSMJ19%% must be deleted.  For example, if P=[2,3,4]%%ZSMJ20%% and the number 3%%ZSMJ21%% has to be deleted, once the event is processed  P%%ZSMJ22%% will become [2,4]%%ZSMJ23%%.

Insert:  a number not present in P%%ZSMJ24%% must be inserted into P%%ZSMJ25%% before some other number present in P%%ZSMJ26%%.  For example, if P=[4,3,2,1]%%ZSMJ27%% and the number 9%%ZSMJ28%% must be inserted before the number 1%%ZSMJ29%%,  once the event is processed  P%%ZSMJ30%% will become [4,3,2,9,1]%%ZSMJ31%%.

Query:  the length of the longest common subarray between P∞%%ZSMJ32%% and A∞%%ZSMJ33%% must be computed,  where A%%ZSMJ34%% is an array given in the query.  For example, if P=[1,2,3,4]%%ZSMJ35%% and A=[3,2]%%ZSMJ36%%, then the longest common subarray between P∞%%ZSMJ37%% and A∞%%ZSMJ38%% is [2,3]%%ZSMJ39%%,  so the answer to the query is 2%%ZSMJ40%%.
Are you ready for this challenge?
input: The first line contains an integer N%%ZSMJ41%% (1≤N≤5⋅105%%ZSMJ42%%) indicating the initial length of P%%ZSMJ43%%.
The second line contains N%%ZSMJ44%% different integers P1,P2,…,PN%%ZSMJ45%% (1≤Pi≤106%%ZSMJ46%% for i=1,2,…,N%%ZSMJ47%%).
The third line contains an integer E%%ZSMJ48%% (1≤E≤5⋅105%%ZSMJ49%%) representing the number of events that need to be processed.
Each of the next E%%ZSMJ50%% lines describes an event, in the order they must be processed. The content of the line depends on the event, as follows:

Delete:  the line contains the character '-' (minus sign) and an integer X%%ZSMJ51%% (1≤X≤106%%ZSMJ52%%, and X∈P%%ZSMJ53%%), denoting that X%%ZSMJ54%% must be deleted from P%%ZSMJ55%%.  It is guaranteed that  after the removal P%%ZSMJ56%% does not become empty.

Insert:  the line contains the character '+' (plus sign) and two integers Y%%ZSMJ57%% and Z%%ZSMJ58%%  (1≤Y,Z≤106%%ZSMJ59%%, Y∉P%%ZSMJ60%%, and Z∈P%%ZSMJ61%%),  denoting that Y%%ZSMJ62%% must be inserted into P%%ZSMJ63%% immediately to the left of Z%%ZSMJ64%%.

Query:  the line contains the character '?' (question mark), a positive integer K%%ZSMJ65%%, and K%%ZSMJ66%% integers A1,A2,…,AK%%ZSMJ67%%  (1≤Ai≤106%%ZSMJ68%% for i=1,2,…,K%%ZSMJ69%%),  indicating that the length of the longest common subarray between P∞%%ZSMJ70%% and A∞%%ZSMJ71%% must be computed.  It is guaranteed that the input contains at least one query, and the sum of  K%%ZSMJ72%% across all the queries  is at most 106%%ZSMJ73%%.
output: Output a line for each query, with an integer indicating the length of the longest common subarray between P∞%%ZSMJ74%% and A∞%%ZSMJ75%%, or the character '*' (asterisk) if the length of the longest common subarray is larger than 1018%%ZSMJ76%%.
